Of every R100 you spend at Shoprite, most goes straight back out: to the farmers and factories that made the food, to cashiers and drivers, and for rent, electricity and fuel. What's left before interest and tax is the trading profit: R16.2 billion on R270.8 billion of sales in its last financial year, a margin of just under 6%. So it doesn't get rich from one trolley. It gets rich from millions of them: about R6 in every R100, on about R5 billion of sales a week.

Full story: "How Shoprite Makes Money: R6 of Every R100 (and Why It's in Every Town)" on the Money From Zero channel.
